understand.concept: time.h provides time-related types and functions such as time, difftime, localtime, gmtime, mktime and strftime. These functions represent calendar time and convert between time representations; availability and range depend on the implementation.
understand.whyItMatters: Time handling involves time zones, daylight-saving transitions, representation ranges and formatting rules. Programs should avoid assuming every timestamp or local-time conversion is universally representable.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: time obtains the current calendar time. localtime converts it to local broken-down time, and strftime formats it into a bounded character array. The example checks failure results.

practise.guidedTask: Explain why the program checks time, localtime and strftime separately.
practise.independentTask: Write a program that measures elapsed time with difftime and formats a local calendar time.
hints: The pointer returned by localtime may refer to static storage and can be overwritten by later calls; use safer alternatives where available.
strftime returns zero when the output does not fit or no characters are produced.
Do not assume local civil time is monotonic for measuring elapsed durations.
